attribution: Lumi additions: Stone Age and prehistory. Written for Lumi. Not part of the Marble Skill Taxonomy.

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Long Ago and Today
topics.description: Some things in daily life are new, and some ideas are very old. Long ago means a time before the people who are alive now, further back than grandparents and old photos.
evidence: Sort pictures or objects into long ago and today
Name one thing that has changed since their grandparents were children
Say that long ago is further back than their own birthday
topics.assessmentPrompt: If you asked the child what long ago means, could they give an example of something from the past and something from today?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: What Is Prehistory
topics.description: Prehistory is the long stretch of human time before people wrote things down. We learn about it from objects, bones, and pictures left in the ground, not from books written at the time.
evidence: Say that prehistory comes before written history
Explain that there are no diaries from the very first people
Name an object, rather than a book, as a clue from prehistory
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child explain that prehistory means the time before writing, and that we use objects as clues?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Early Humans and Where They Lived
topics.description: Early humans moved across Africa, Europe, and Asia. They lived in caves and in camps in the open, close to water, stone, and animals they could hunt.
evidence: Say that early humans lived in more than one part of the world
Name a cave or a camp as a kind of home
Give a reason people stayed near water or animals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child describe where early humans lived and one reason a place was a good camp?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Hunter-Gatherers
topics.description: For most of prehistory people did not farm. They hunted animals, caught fish, and gathered plants, nuts, and shellfish. They often moved with the seasons.
evidence: Explain hunting and gathering in their own words
Name two foods people could find without a farm
Say why a group might move camp
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child explain how hunter-gatherers got food, and why they did not stay in one field all year?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: First Tools: Stone, Bone and Wood
topics.description: The first tools were made by shaping stone, bone, antler, and wood. A hand axe or a scraper could cut meat, scrape skins, and shape other tools. Stone tools are why this time is called the Stone Age.
evidence: Name stone, bone, or wood as a tool material
Give one job a stone tool could do
Say why this time is called the Stone Age
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child name a Stone Age tool material and one way people used it?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Discovering Fire
topics.description: Fire changed camp life. People used it to keep warm, to scare off animals, to see in the dark, and later to cook food. Tending a fire took care and teamwork.
evidence: Name two uses of fire in a camp
Say that fire needed someone to look after it
Compare raw food and cooked food in a simple way
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child give two reasons fire mattered to early humans?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Cave Paintings
topics.description: People painted animals and signs on cave walls. Famous caves include Lascaux in France and Chauvet in France. The paintings used minerals, charcoal, and brushes made from hair or sticks. They show what people noticed and cared about.
evidence: Name Lascaux or Chauvet as a painted cave
Say that many paintings show animals
Name a material used to make the paint
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child describe what cave painters showed, and name one famous cave?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Mammoths and Ice Age Animals
topics.description: During colder Ice Age times, woolly mammoths, reindeer, bison, and cave bears lived in parts of Europe and Asia. People hunted some of them and painted them. Mammoths later died out.
evidence: Name a mammoth as an Ice Age animal
Say one way a mammoth was suited to the cold
Say that people met these animals long ago
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child name an Ice Age animal and one clue that the climate was cold?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Old, Middle and New Stone Age
topics.description: Historians split the Stone Age into three stretches. The Old Stone Age was the longest, with hunting and gathering. The Middle Stone Age came as the ice retreated and people used more small tools. The New Stone Age brought farming in many places.
evidence: Name the Old, Middle, and New Stone Age in order
Match hunting and gathering with the older stretch
Match farming with the New Stone Age
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child put Old, Middle, and New Stone Age in order and say what changed?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: The First Farmers
topics.description: In the New Stone Age, the Neolithic, people in some places began to grow wheat and barley and to keep sheep, goats, and cattle. Farming meant storing food and often staying in one village. It did not begin everywhere at the same time.
evidence: Say that farming means growing food and keeping animals
Name one crop or animal kept by early farmers
Give one way village life differed from moving camps
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child explain what the first farmers did, and one change it made to daily life?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Skara Brae Village
topics.description: Skara Brae is a Neolithic village in Orkney, Scotland. Stone houses were sunk into the ground, with beds and dressers made of stone. A storm uncovered it in 1850. It shows how some farmers lived about 5,000 years ago.
evidence: Place Skara Brae in Scotland
Describe a stone house with stone furniture
Say that the village belonged to farmers, not to people alive today
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child say where Skara Brae is and one thing the houses show about village life?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Stonehenge and Standing Stones
topics.description: Stonehenge in England is a circle of huge standing stones raised in the New Stone Age and the early Bronze Age. People dragged some stones from far away. Circles like this were meeting places. We still ask what ceremonies happened there.
evidence: Describe Stonehenge as a circle of large stones
Say that building it took many people
Say that historians are still not certain about every use
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child describe Stonehenge and say why moving the stones was hard work?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Bronze Age Changes
topics.description: After the New Stone Age, people in many places learned to mix copper and tin to make bronze. Bronze made stronger tools and weapons. Trade grew, because tin and copper are not found everywhere. Stone tools did not disappear overnight.
evidence: Say that bronze is a metal made by mixing copper and tin
Name one way bronze tools differed from stone tools
Say that trade helped people get the metals
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child explain what changed when people started to use bronze?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: How We Know: Archaeology and Artefacts
topics.description: Archaeology is the careful study of things people left behind. An artefact is an object people made, such as a flint tool or a pot. Archaeologists record where each object was found. Digging slowly keeps the clues in order.
evidence: Explain artefact as an object people made
Say that the place an object is found is part of the clue
Describe archaeology as careful digging and recording, not treasure hunting
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child explain how archaeologists learn about people who left no writing?

topics.subject: History
topics.name: Stone Age Timeline
topics.description: A Stone Age timeline runs from the Old Stone Age, through the Middle and New Stone Age, into the Bronze Age, and then toward the first civilisations that wrote things down. Ancient Egypt's long written history begins after these prehistoric stretches in this story of the past.
evidence: Order Old Stone Age, New Stone Age, and Bronze Age
Place hunter-gatherers before farmers on a simple line
Say that ancient Egypt's written history comes later on the same line
topics.assessmentPrompt: Could the child put the Stone Age stretches and the Bronze Age in order, and say that ancient Egypt comes later in this story?
